messages.content: Write the invitation copy for a webinar about database performance tuning. Around 200 words.

output:
**Your slowest query is probably your own fault.**

Most database slowdowns aren't a hardware problem. They come from a query that looked fine in staging, then met a table with 40 million rows and no covering index.

On **[DATE, TIME]**, join **[SPEAKER, TITLE]** for 45 minutes on performance tuning — the practical kind. No vendor pitch.

We'll work through real EXPLAIN plans, live:

- Reading an execution plan without guessing, including where the cost estimates lie to you
- Why your index isn't being used, and the four usual reasons
- Catching N+1 queries from the database side instead of the app
- When to stop tuning and start denormalizing

Bring a slow query. The last 15 minutes are yours, and we'll take as many questions from the queue as we can get through.

Who it's for: backend engineers, DBAs, and anyone who's been paged at 3 a.m. because p99 latency doubled after a deploy. Examples are in Postgres and MySQL, though the ideas port to most engines.

Free to attend. We record it, so register even if the time doesn't work — the link lands in your inbox the next morning.

**[Save my seat →]**

Placeholders in brackets are yours to fill; swap the Postgres/MySQL line if your audience runs something else.
